steps.text: In a large pot of salted boiling water, cook pasta until al dente, rinse under cold water and drain.

Place eggs in a saucepan and cover completely with cold water. Bring water to a boil. Cover, remove from heat, and let eggs stand in hot water for 10 to 12 minutes. Remove from hot water, cool, peel and chop.
Whisk together the salad dressing, sugar, vinegar, salt and pepper.
In a large bowl, combine the pasta, eggs, peas, green onion, pickles, celery and cheese. Pour dressing over salad; mix well and chill before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Pea Salad II
raw_recipe.description: This salad has a definite sweetness about it. A bit of sugar is added to the dressing and sweet pickles are tossed in with the peas, onions, celery, eggs and cheese. Makes six generous servings.
raw_recipe.name: Pea Salad II

review.reviewBody: I have made this recipe many times. I am not a cheese fan, so I eliminate the cheese and I add dill to it. GREAT quick and easy salad to have for a quick bite or to take to carry in's

This is so good I made it twice in one week. Love the dressing, it's perfect! I left out the sweet pickle, as we don't like ours too sweet. I added some chopped red bell pepper that I had on hand for additional flavor and color. I also used canned peas that I had refrigerated a couple of hours before hand so they'd stay firm. We prefer canned peas over frozen. This is staying in the rotation!

Delicious…. I didn’t add the eggs because I was in a hurry. I used dill pickles instead of the sweet and added a mini red pepper. Oh and I also sprinkled it with about 2 TBSP of dry ranch to get more ranchie flavor.

Excellent ! Followed almost exactly. Based on what I had: used mayo, white vinegar and sweet pickle relish. Used a little bit more than the 1/4 cup. Tastes great. Oh ….. fresh peas from the local farm 👍🏻👍🏻

This was a nice pasta salad with a veggie thrown in. Especially since I had to tweak it a bit for what I had on hand. Parmesan dressing instead of ranch, apple cider vinegar, dehyd. onions, and pickle relish. After all that, it still ended up tasty! I agree though that 1/4C dressing is really not enough. I had to add more to make it moist enough. Probably used a little more of the peas too. And sprinkled in some dried oregano for a little extra flavor. All in all, a tasty salad for a warm summer's day.

Yum-my! Had to make a few adjustments, though. No onions, because I can't eat them, used Rice Vinegar because I didn't have white wine vinegar, and used canned peas because that's what I was trying to use up. I used mayo because I don't like Ranch dressing and also doubled the dressing after reading other reviews. This is a complete meal: protein, starch, vegetables. It's filling but light: a definite keeper!

Granted, I was already hungry, but when I finished preparing this salad, I ate about ten spoonfuls. It was so delicious, I couldn't help myself. Please note that if you have a tendency to add slightly more peas or pasta, you will need more ranch dressing. 1/4 cup of the dressing doesn't go very far; be prepared to add more, if necessary.

Oh my, so good and easy! My husband loved this and proclaimed it to be his favorite pasta salad. 
I ran out of ranch dressing (I doubled the pasta) and mixed miracle whip, white vinegar and sugar as a dressing stretch. Used pickle relish as a sub for the cut up pickles and no celery.
Will make again with celery and maybe red onion.
Thanks Amanda

Fantastic salad!! Didn't have any celery so chopped up a med. red bell pepper for crunch, added sliced black olives & served it on a bed of Romaine lettuce. So good there were no leftovers. I will make this again
soon!!!! Thanks for the recipe.
This seemed really dry with only 1/4 cup of dressing, so doubled that, still seemed dry, so also added 1/4 cup mayo. It was okay, but rather bland for my taste.
I left out the pickles and used small cubed cheddar cheese. Also added red bell pepper.

I had something similar to this at a potluck. Nobody knew who brought it so I went on a search. This is the closest recipe I could find anywhere and I tried it. I absolutely love it. You can tweak it with more pickles or eggs or pasta, whatever tickles your fancy. I will be definitely making this in the summer salad rotation!!

I really liked the combination of ingredients, but I wasn’t crazy about the dressing, it simply didn’t coat the pasta really well. And I guess I was looking for more of the Ranch dressing flavor. Pretty good, but I’d do some tweaking if I made again.

I thought this was very good. I should have made more as I really didn't think about the quantity. I felt the dressing was very flavorful, maybe I could have made a little more but overall, I thought everything was very good.

Sigh - Lucky for me this is a very forgiving recipe. Having said that, if you happen to find out at the last minute that you don't have any ranch dressing, lite blue cheese works really well. And I doubled the sauce since it seemed to dry to me, but thanks so much for the post. We'll do this again and again!
Really liked this recipe as a basic starter. I thought it was a little bland, so added some rosemary and thyme. Perked it right up.
This was really delicious. I made it according to the recipe. Make sure to use a good ranch dressing (Hidden Valley is our favorite!). My family loved it.
